newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Jan deficit on national account up 40.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain Jan deficit on national account up 40.3 pct.

text.p: Spain's January central state deficit on a national account basis rose to a provisional 399.5 billion pesetas ($2.8 billion), 40.3-percent higher than the same period a year ago, the Economy Ministry said on Wednesday.
January's cash basis deficit rose to 376.5 billion pesetas in 1996, up from 151.9 billion in January 1995.

NOTE - The figures relate to central government finances only. GBR = government borrowing requirement.

A spokesman said the deficit on a national account basis was provisional because the government borrowing requirement needed a small adjustement before it adhered to the exact definition of the deficit on a national account basis.
Earlier, Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said the deterioration was due to technical factors and was not relevant.
The central government public deficit on a national account basis is the one considered relevant for the Maastricht Treaty, which sets out the economic goals to join the European single currency.
It takes into account accrued revenues and expenditures for a given period, while the deficit on a cash basis registers actual money movements during a given month. -- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
